title: Observability Ingest Buffer, Drift Scoring, and Tiered Burn-Rate Suppression
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight ingest buffer ("Trace Inlet") for span/metric/log pipelines that attaches tier and sampling hints, computes a continuous drift score for SLO-affecting metrics, and enables a tiered burn-rate suppression layer to reduce noisy paging for low-impact drift anomalies.

Context: Recent incidents showed a class of slow-degrading latency issues that do not trip instant thresholds but slowly increase error-rate/latency across services. Our current burn-rate + alerting configuration triggers noisy pages for minor transient spikes and causes oncall fatigue. We need an ingestion-side capability to annotate telemetry with routing hints, a metric drift scoring signal to detect slow regressions, and a suppression policy that factors customer tier and drift confidence when deciding to page.

Goals:
- Add a near-ingest span/metric hook (Trace Inlet) that: captures request-level attributes (route, model variant, customer_tier), normalizes latency/error buckets, and emits a lightweight drift signal alongside existing spans.
- Implement a continuous drift scorer that runs in the metrics pipeline and outputs a 0..100 drift_confidence label per SLO window. The scorer should use EWMA of percentile deltas and spectral-change heuristics to be robust to seasonality.
- Introduce tiered burn-rate suppression policy: when drift_confidence < threshold for a given tier, suppress paging and instead escalate to quieter channels (Slack + Ops dashboard), with automatic re-evaluation and ramp-up logic.

Non-goals: full model replacement for anomaly detection (we'll iterate with heuristics first), changing existing SLI definitions, or removing any existing burn-rate alerts before careful canarying.

Design notes:
- Trace Inlet lives as a thin transformation node in the ingest path (before Kafka topic x-observability). It will be written in Go to match the existing ingestion stack and keep CPU overhead low.
- Drift scoring algorithm: combine short-window (5m) median shift, long-window (24h) baseline comparison, and a seasonality-aware spectral delta. Output: drift_confidence (stringified integer 0-100) and drift_reason tags (list encoded as CSV).
- Suppression logic: map customer_tier -> drift_threshold and paging_policy. Example mapping: enterprise: threshold 30 -> immediate page when burn-rate > configured; standard: threshold 60 -> require sustained burn-rate and drift_confidence >=60 to page; trial: threshold 80 -> never page automatically, only create ticket.
- Rollout plan: enable Trace Inlet in dev -> internal staging -> 2 canary services -> roll to all non-prod namespaces -> opt-in customers -> full prod. Suppression policy initially only affects new tiered paging rule; existing burn-rate alerts will retain current behavior until controlled cutover.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Trace Inlet deployed to staging and processing 100% of staging traffic with <1% CPU overhead on ingestion nodes.
2) Drift scorer output visible in metrics platform (label drift_confidence) and recorded for 90% of SLO windows.
3) Tiered suppression can be toggled per-namespace via feature flag and logs show expected suppression decisions in canary runs.
4) No regressions in SLI coverage and no missed P0 incidents during the opt-in canary phase.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Drift Score Feed" showing per-service median drift_confidence, top drift_reasons, and correlation heatmap with burn-rate alerts.
- Add annotations to existing latency/error dashboards to show suppression decisions and the inbound Trace Inlet sampling rates.

Security & compliance: Trace Inlet must not materialize PII. Any request metadata that could be sensitive must be redacted at source. We will reuse existing KMS policies for encryption-in-flight and at-rest in Kafka topics.

Testing plan: unit tests for drift scorer; e2e with synthetic slow-degradation traffic; chaos test to ensure suppression does not block paging on true outages; load test to ensure ingestion overhead is acceptable.

Notes for implementers: link to prototype design doc and infra diagram in links. Use existing ingest-side metrics and the telemetry-sdk wrappers to minimize instrumentation churn.
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting complete. Agreed to prototype drift scorer using EWMA+spectral delta. Action: Marco to produce spike PR for Trace Inlet skeleton (ENG-451238-1).
2026-03-03: Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/4217. Initial Trace Inlet emits drift_confidence as tag on spans. CPU overhead measured at ~0.6% in local perf harness.

2026-03-05: Design review feedback from Priya (SRE): require additional debug logging and a circuit-breaker to disable Trace Inlet per-cluster. Priya also requested telemetry for suppress_count and suppressed_incidents_count.

2026-03-08: Implemented drift scorer v0.1. Ran synthetic slow-degrade test; scorer produced a rising drift_confidence that correlates with 95th percentile increase. Next: integrate with alerting engine to annotate candidate burn events.

2026-03-10: Product review with Dan (PM). Agreed on tier mappings and suppression defaults. Dan asked for a 'safety ramp' that requires 2 corroborating signals (burn-rate + drift_confidence) before suppression for standard tier. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed redaction approach and approved; recommended adding automated unit test that asserts no raw user IDs are present in emitted tags.
